title: Tensor product with a separably closed field has a unique minimal prime
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $L/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Then the ring $K\otimes_k L$ has a unique minimal prime; consequently $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k L)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-tensor-reduction] to pass to the reductions R,S of the two algebraic-closure base changes. They are domains and their tensor product has a spectrum homeomorphic to the original tensor product.

Over the algebraically closed base, any two tensor elements have finite supports. Adjoin their right-hand coefficients to obtain a finite type domain D inside S. Tensoring its inclusion with R is injective by Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algclosed-finite-type-tensor-domain] to R and D; a product zero then forces one of the two elements zero. Nontriviality gives that R tensor S is a domain.

The spectrum of a domain is irreducible. Transport this instance through the homeomorphism. PrimeSpectrum.irreducibleSpace_iff_isPrime_nilradical makes the nilradical of K tensor L prime. Ideal.radical_minimalPrimes and Ideal.minimalPrimes_eq_subsingleton_self say that it is the unique minimal prime. Finally an irreducible space is connected. The affine scheme carrier is definitionally PrimeSpectrum.
